# Feature: Task-Fidelity Harness

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-049
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_task_fidelity.md` (§1 "The finding"; §5 CLI surface `pnpm eval:tasks`; §7 "Target trace" and "Sequencing"; §9 Testing Strategy; §11 Success Criteria)

Give Yantra an outcome-level gate: a harness that measures whether a run delivered **what the user asked for**, not only whether each tool behaved. Then record a baseline of today's pipeline before FEAT-050–053 change it.

Today there is no such measurement. Two runs of the identical goal (`20260919T231319Z` and `20260925T130634Z`) chose opposite strategies, reported two different "lowest prices", and neither delivered the expected table. Every later feature in this plan claims to move a row of §11. Without a harness, each claim is one more anecdote.

The harness has two tiers over one shared set of generic fixture sites:

- **The deterministic tier** (`@no-llm`, all three OSes, gates CI). A scripted agent drives the real tool pipeline through `runAgenticTask` against loopback fixture sites, with a scripted search provider and fault injection. Each scenario asserts structural facts about the completed run directory and an independent server-side request log.
- **The agentic tier** (`pnpm eval:tasks`, on demand, never in CI). It runs the same scenarios with a real model three times per scenario. It scores field coverage, constraint fidelity, source fidelity, citation validity, honesty, cost, and stability, and it writes `scorecard.json` and `scorecard.md`.

Acceptance requires all of the following:

- Six fixture patterns (`faceted-listing`, `structured-listing`, `client-rendered-listing`, `challenge-interstitial`, `article`, `multi-table`) are served by the loopback e2e host under distinct reserved hostnames. All of them are rendered from one checked-in truth dataset, so the pages and the ground truth cannot diverge.
- A test-only scripted search provider, injected through the existing provider seam, returns deterministic SERPs that point at the fixtures. It injects `challenge-on-concurrency`, `empty`, and `timeout` faults by throwing the **real** core error classes.
- The deterministic tier passes on the current tree, on all three OSes, inside `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:no-llm`.
- Every deterministic expectation names its **owner** (`current`, `FEAT-048`, or `FEAT-050`–`FEAT-053`). A capability whose owner has not landed is pinned at its observed **baseline**. When the owner lands, it removes itself from one `PENDING_OWNERS` set, and its **target** assertions become live and gating. A pending expectation whose target already passes fails the suite, so nobody can forget to flip it.
- `pnpm eval:tasks` runs the agentic tier with the shared model flag vocabulary and writes a schema-validated scorecard. A baseline scorecard summary on today's pipeline is committed, and its headline numbers are recorded in the plan's revision log.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope: the fixture sites, the host mapping, the scripted search provider, the scripted agent, the expectation ratchet, the deterministic tier, the scorer, the agentic runner, and the baseline. Production code changes only for two harness seams (TASK-003), both inert in production.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:

- Every behavior the harness _measures_ but does not build: typed causes and notices (**FEAT-048**); politeness, breaker, cache, evidence IDs, `limit: 0`, challenge classification, and the shared browser (**FEAT-050**); shape, records, links, structured data, and tables (**FEAT-051**); the task contract and research browsing (**FEAT-052**); tables, citations, and constraints in the Brief (**FEAT-053**). The harness pins their targets. It never implements them.
- The deterministic `ask` / `research --no-llm` pipelines. Plan §7 defers their adoption of the run services, so the harness drives agentic runs only (recorded in TODO).
- Click and fill interaction (FEAT-031–040, gated by the widget gauntlet). The harness only _counts_ `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` handoffs (plan §7).
- Gating CI on agentic scores. Agentic scores are observational, as the ⚠ marks in plan §11 say.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No relational store. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. Every entity is harness-local TypeScript under `e2e/task-fidelity/`, plus a Zod schema for the scorecard artifact. Nothing here is added to `@yantra/protocol`, because the scorecard is a dev-only artifact and not a run-artifact format users own.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`InventoryItem`** (`fixtures/inventory.ts`; the single source of truth for every listing fixture):
  - `id` (string, stable, e.g. `itm-07`) NOT NULL UNIQUE
  - `title` (string): a fictional make, model, and trim. No real brand or site name.
  - `condition` (`'new' | 'used'`), `year` (int), `trim` (string), `drivetrain` (`'AWD' | 'FWD'`)
  - `price` (int, whole currency units), `msrp` (int)
  - `seller` (string, fictional), `distanceMi` (number)
  - `exteriorColor`, `interiorColor` (string). They appear **only** on detail pages, as in the motivating run, so collecting them requires following detail links.
  - The dataset holds 14 items, so a listing page shows several cards and pagination exists. Some items deliberately fail one filter (FWD, used, or another trim), which makes constraint fidelity measurable.
- **`TaskSite`** (`fixtures/sites.ts`):
  - `name`: the pattern name, unique (`faceted-listing`, …). It doubles as the hostname label.
  - `host`: `<name>.yantra.test`. RFC 2606 reserves `.test`, so it can never resolve publicly.
  - `pattern` (string): the one-sentence generic pattern this site encodes. The census requires it to be unique.
  - `provenance` (`{ run?: string; gap?: 'G2' | 'G3' | 'G10' | … }`): evidence for why the pattern exists. Rendered only into the page's header comment.
  - `render(path, query): { status, contentType, body } | null`: pure and deterministic, reading from `inventory.ts` or a static article/table corpus.
- **`TruthRow`** (derived, never hand-written): `{ itemId, key: { title, seller }, fields: Record<FieldName, string>, satisfies: Record<FilterName, boolean>, detailUrl, listingUrl }`. It is derived from `InventoryItem` by the same module that renders the pages.
- **`RequestLogEntry`** (fixture server, in memory): `{ host, path, query, method, userAgentClass: 'http' | 'browser', at }`. The harness counts network fetches from this log, independently of anything the run reports about itself.
- **`ScriptedSerp`** (`search/scripted-provider.ts`): `{ match: string | RegExp, results: SearchResult[] }[]` per scenario, plus `faults: SearchFault[]`.
  - `SearchFault` is a discriminated union: `{ kind: 'challenge-on-concurrency' }`, `{ kind: 'empty'; onCall: number[] }`, `{ kind: 'timeout'; onCall: number[] }`, `{ kind: 'challenge'; onCall: number[] }`.
  - The provider records `{ call, query, startedAt, endedAt, outcome, peakConcurrency }` per call.
- **`ScriptStep`** (`agent/scripted-provider.ts`), a discriminated union:
  - `{ kind: 'call'; tool: string; params: Record<string, unknown> | ((ctx: ScriptContext) => Record<string, unknown> | null) }`. A resolver returning `null` means "this move is unreachable from the evidence so far". The step is recorded as `unreachable`, and no tool call is made. A resolver never invents a URL.
  - `{ kind: 'parallel'; steps: readonly ScriptStep[] }` issues calls concurrently, as Pi does for multi-tool turns.
  - `ScriptContext` exposes the prior tool results (parsed `details` and model text), plus helper pickers (`linksOfKind`, `recordsFrom`, `firstUrlFromSearch`). These read **only** fields a result actually carries.
- **`Scenario`** (`scenarios/*.ts`):
  - `id` (string, unique), `sites: TaskSite['name'][]`, `command: 'ask' | 'research' | 'do'`
  - `goal` (string): fixture-native, with the required source named by host.
  - `contract` (`{ deliverable, requiredFields[], filters[{ name, value }], requiredSources[], ranking?, limit? }`). This is the harness's own ground-truth contract for scoring. It is **not** passed to the run, because FEAT-052 owns how a run declares one.
  - `userLocation` (string | null), `serps: ScriptedSerp`, `budgets?: Partial<AgentBudgetConfig>`
  - `script: readonly ScriptStep[]` (deterministic tier only), `expectations: readonly Expectation[]`, `tiers: ('deterministic' | 'agentic')[]`
- **`Expectation`** (`expectations.ts`):
  - `id` (string, unique within the scenario)
  - `owner` (`'current' | 'FEAT-048' | 'FEAT-050' | 'FEAT-051' | 'FEAT-052' | 'FEAT-053'`)
  - `measure: (run: ScenarioRun) => unknown`: a pure read of the completed run
  - `target: Matcher`: the contract the owner must meet
  - `baseline?: Matcher`: required when `owner` is pending, forbidden when `owner === 'current'`
  - `note` (string): one line naming the plan gap (`G2`, `G10`, …) or the §11 row it pins
- **`PENDING_OWNERS`** (`expectations.ts`): `ReadonlySet<Owner>`. The only switch that decides baseline versus target. At the time of writing it holds `FEAT-050`–`FEAT-053`, plus `FEAT-048` if that feature has not landed when this one is implemented.
- **`ScenarioRun`** (`runner.ts`): everything a measure may read, captured after the run has fully finalized.
  - `outcome` (the `AgenticTaskOutcome`) and `runDir`
  - `artifacts`: parsed `manifest.json`, `brief.json` or `document.json`, `tool-calls.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl`, `usage.json`, `report.md`, and `run-health.json` when present. Each absent file is `null`, never a throw.
  - `toolResults` (the scripted agent's received results), `unreachable` (step labels)
  - `requests` (`RequestLogEntry[]`), `searchCalls`, `browserLaunches` (harness-counted), `rankSignals` (recording sink)
- **`ScoreCard`** (Zod schema `scorecard-schema.ts`; persisted as `scorecard.json`):
  - `schema_version` (literal `1`), `generated_at` (ISO), `git_sha` (string | null), `prompt_version` (string)
  - `model`: `{ provider, id, thinking: string | null }`
  - `runs_per_scenario` (int ≥ 1)
  - `scenarios[]`:
    - `{ id, runs[], aggregate }`
    - each run: `{ run_id, outcome_kind, field_coverage, constraint_fidelity, source_fidelity, citation_validity, honesty, cost, interaction_required, delivered_row_keys[] }`
    - `aggregate`: the median of each score plus `stability`
  - `totals`: `{ runs, wall_ms, cost_usd: number | null, navigations, browser_launches }`
  - Each score is `{ value: number | null, numerator, denominator, detail: string[] }`. A score is `null` when its denominator is 0, such as citation validity when nothing was cited. It is never silently 1.0.

### Relationships

- `InventoryItem` 1:1 `TruthRow` (derived). `TaskSite` 1:N rendered pages. `Scenario` N:M `TaskSite` via `sites`.
- `Scenario` 1:N `Expectation`. `Expectation` N:1 owner. `PENDING_OWNERS` decides which matcher runs.
- One deterministic scenario execution yields one `ScenarioRun`. One agentic scenario yields `runs_per_scenario` `ScenarioRun`s and one scorecard entry.

### Indexes & Constraints

- Scenario IDs, expectation IDs (per scenario), and site names and patterns are each unique. The census enforces all four.
- Every pending owner has at least one expectation with a `baseline`. An owner that is not pending has none, so stale baselines are deleted when their owner lands.
- No fixture body (HTML, JSON-LD, script) or fixture TypeScript value contains a real site or brand token. Site names may appear only in a header provenance comment (memory → General).
- The deterministic tier never contacts a non-loopback address. Any request the host mapping does not cover fails closed with a loud error (TASK-001).

## 5. Implementation Tasks

> **Running the harness.** Per memory, the e2e workspace resolves `@yantra/core` and `@yantra/agent` from built `dist/`, so run `npx turbo run build` before trusting any result. A targeted run is `cd e2e && npx vitest run task-fidelity`. The repo-wide `npx turbo run lint typecheck` plus the full e2e suite is the gate.

### TASK-001: Host-routed task-site server with reserved hostnames, and the `faceted-listing` pattern

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Host mapping.** Each site is reached at `http://<name>.yantra.test/…`, so hostname-based policy (host budgets, required-source checks, ranking) sees distinct hosts, as it does in production. Today every fixture shares `127.0.0.1`, which would make source fidelity trivially true. All mapping lives in the harness:
    - `mappedRequestFn(port)` wraps `node:http` `request`. It rewrites a `*.yantra.test` target to `127.0.0.1:<port>` and preserves the `Host` header. `HttpFetcher` already accepts `requestFn`.
    - `hostMappedBrowserProvider(inner, port)` decorates a `BrowserProvider`. It appends `--host-resolver-rules=MAP *.yantra.test 127.0.0.1:<port>, EXCLUDE localhost` to `extraArgs` on every `launch`, delegates every other member unchanged, and counts successful launches. It must not narrow the provider's type.
    - Any request to a non-loopback, non-`yantra.test` host throws `HarnessEgressError` naming the host. Chrome gets `MAP * ~NOTFOUND` after the fixture rule. The deterministic tier is hermetic by construction, not by convention.
  - **Server.** `serveTaskSites()` listens on an ephemeral loopback port, routes by the `Host` header's hostname label to the `TaskSite` renderer, and serves `User-agent: *\nAllow: /` at `/robots.txt` on every host. It appends a `RequestLogEntry` for every request, including robots, which is flagged. It returns `{ port, origin(name), requests(), reset(), close() }`. Unknown hosts and paths return 404 and are logged. Reuse the listen/close helpers factored out of `e2e/fixtures/serve.ts`.
  - **`faceted-listing` renderer.** All pages are rendered from `inventory.ts`.
    - `/new/results`: server-rendered repeated cards, 6 per page. Each card has a title link, a plain-text price block (`50,265` / `MSRP $50,255` / `Fees included`), a seller **link**, a distance (`27.0 mi away`), and a detail link. A facet sidebar lists `Drivetrain: AWD (n)`, `FWD (n)`, and trims, each with a count, as links to variants of the current URL (`?drivetrain=AWD`). Pagination links (`?page=2`) complete the page.
    - `/new/results?drivetrain=AWD`: filters the cards server-side.
    - `/vehicle/<id>`: a detail page with a `<dl>` attribute table (exterior color, interior color, drivetrain, condition, stock number) and a price.
    - The header comment cites run `20260925T130634Z` and gaps G2/G3 as provenance only.
  - The **G2 regression card** is the plain first card: its price is plain text, and its title and seller are links (plan §9).
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`e2e/task-fidelity-harness.spec.ts`, `@no-llm`):
  - Through the production `HttpFetcher` with `mappedRequestFn`, each `faceted-listing` route returns 200 with the expected content type. An unknown host returns 404, and both requests are logged with the right host and path.
  - Through real Chrome via `hostMappedBrowserProvider`, `http://faceted-listing.yantra.test/new/results` renders and its `Host` routing works. The decorator counts exactly one launch and preserves every delegated member.
  - Egress: `mappedRequestFn` to `example.org` throws `HarnessEgressError`, and Chrome navigation to a non-fixture host fails without reaching the network.
  - Truth agreement: for every item, the rendered detail page contains its truth colors, and the listing page contains its price and seller. The AWD facet count equals the number of AWD truth rows.
  - Determinism: two renders of every route are byte-identical.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the task-fidelity harness (fixture hosting and host mapping).
- **Verify**: `npx turbo run build`, then `cd e2e && npx vitest run task-fidelity-harness` passes on Windows. The CI matrix covers macOS and Ubuntu.

### TASK-002: The remaining fixture patterns and the fixture census

- [ ] **Implementation** (all rendered from the same dataset or corpus; each with a header provenance comment and a unique one-sentence `pattern`):

    - `large-main`: wrapped in `<main>`, padded past 10 KB with boilerplate.

  - `article`: long-form prose (a checked-in corpus of about 1,500 words) with a byline and `datePublished` JSON-LD. It guards the Readability path.
  - `multi-table`: a page whose first `<table>` is an unrelated summary and whose **second** table holds the answer (closes TODO line 214 once FEAT-051 lands).
  - **Census** (`e2e/task-fidelity-harness.spec.ts`):

    - Every site has a provenance entry, and the provenance text appears only inside the leading header comment of each rendered page.

    - Every `TruthRow` field rendered on a page appears exactly where the truth says it does.

### TASK-003: Two inert production seams: environment leaves and the audit projection

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Why it is needed.** The harness must measure the **production** composition of search, fetch, extraction, ethics, publish, and browser. FEAT-050 rewires exactly that composition (`SearchService`, `DocumentStore`, `PagePool`). A hand-built harness environment would keep measuring the old wiring after FEAT-050 lands, so FEAT-050's targets could never pass in the harness. The harness must therefore call the same composer with different leaves.
  - In `orchestrator.ts`, introduce `interface EnvironmentLeaves` with:
    - `keychain`, `ethicsConfig`, `searchConfig`, `blocklist`
    - `createBrowserProvider(opts) => BrowserProvider`
    - `httpRequestFn?: typeof request`
    - `resolveSearchProvider?: (deps) => Promise<Result<SearchProvider, Error>>`

    `defaultEnvironmentLeaves()` builds today's values (keychain provider, `loadEthicsConfig`, `loadSearchConfig`, `BlocklistImpl.reload`, `createSelectedBrowserProvider`, core `resolveSearchProvider`). `composeDefaultEnvironment(context, runtimeLog, leaves)` reads only from `leaves`. The task controller, fallback fetcher, scrape transport, and nested-workflow providers all go through `leaves.createBrowserProvider`.

  - `AgenticTaskDependencies.environmentLeaves?: Partial<EnvironmentLeaves>` is merged over the defaults. JSDoc states that it is test/embedding-only, applies only when `createEnvironment` is absent, and changes **leaves only**: no policy, budget, sanitizer, consent, or audit enforcement can be replaced through it (memory → Architecture).
  - Export `auditProjectionOf(result: YantraToolResult): unknown` from `adapters/pi/tools/index.ts` and the package index. It returns `createDefaultPiEventMapContext().sanitizePayload(toAgentToolResult(result))`, which is exactly what the Pi seam records. The scripted agent's `tool-calls.jsonl` is therefore produced by the same projection as a real session's, including any FEAT-048 TASK-001 fix. The return type is `unknown`, so no Pi SDK type crosses the package boundary (memory → Project Structure).

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - With no overrides, `defaultEnvironmentLeaves()` is called once per run, and the existing orchestrator suites pass unchanged (characterization).
  - An override for `resolveSearchProvider` is what `web_search` resolves. An override for `httpRequestFn` reaches `web_fetch`'s HTTP tier. An override for `createBrowserProvider` is used by the task controller, `BrowserFallbackFetcher`, and the scrape transport (three spies, one provider).
  - `environmentLeaves` is ignored when `createEnvironment` is supplied, and the test asserts that explicitly.
  - `auditProjectionOf` deep-equals `mapPiEvent(tool_execution_end).output` for a success, a failure, and a rich-content result.
  - The boundary suite still passes: no provider SDK import outside `adapters/pi`, and no core-to-agent import.

### TASK-004: Scripted search provider with fault injection

- [ ] **Implementation** (`search/scripted-provider.ts`, harness-only):
  - `ScriptedSearchProvider implements SearchProvider`.
    - `name` is set per scenario to a real `SearchProviderName`, because the union is closed. Fault scenarios use `duckduckgo`, so any policy keyed on a provider's scraped _kind_ (FEAT-050's gate) applies exactly as it would in production.
    - `search(query, { limit, signal })` matches the scenario's `ScriptedSerp` table in order and returns at most `limit` results, with fixture URLs on `*.yantra.test`.
    - An unmatched query returns `[]`. It never falls through to a real provider.
  - Faults throw the **real** core classes, never structural doubles (memory → Testing):
    - `challenge-on-concurrency`: a call that starts while another is in flight throws `ScrapeSearchError('…', { code: 'anomaly-challenge', … })`. This models G4's observed pattern, where every failure fell inside a concurrent pair.
    - `challenge`, `empty`, and `timeout` on the listed call indices. `empty` throws `ScrapeSearchError` with code `empty-results`. `timeout` waits until the abort signal fires and then rejects as the transport does, or rejects with the provider's timeout code when no signal is wired.
  - The call log records `query`, `startedAt`/`endedAt` from an injected monotonic clock, `outcome`, and `peakConcurrency`. Chaining calls with no overlap is what FEAT-050's serialization will produce.
  - Leaves wiring: `environmentLeaves.resolveSearchProvider = () => ok(provider)`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Two overlapping calls under `challenge-on-concurrency` yield one success and one `ScrapeSearchError` whose `context.code === 'anomaly-challenge'`. Two sequential calls both succeed.
  - `empty` and `timeout` throw on exactly the listed calls. `timeout` honors abort within 50 ms.
  - `limit: 0` returns `[]` without consulting the table, so the provider never pretends to support discovery mode on its own.
  - The call log's `peakConcurrency` is exact.
  - An unmatched query never throws and never reaches the network.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the task-fidelity harness (search faults and what each models).

### TASK-005: Scripted agent and the scenario runner

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `ScriptedAgentProvider implements AgentProvider` (generalized from `ToolDrivingProvider`):
    - On `open`, it builds the run's own wrapped tools with `buildYantraWrappedTools(services)`.
    - On the first `run()`, it executes the scenario script. On any later prompt (the completion nudge), it executes nothing, so the script must publish on its own.
    - For each `call` step, it resolves params against `ScriptContext`. A resolver returning `null` records `unreachable: <label>` and makes no call.
    - It emits `tool_started` with the params, awaits `tool.execute`, and emits `tool_finished` with `output: auditProjectionOf(result)`, `isError: status !== 'ok'`. The audit is projected exactly as Pi projects it (TASK-003).
    - `parallel` steps run with `Promise.all` and emit interleaved events in real completion order.
    - It emits one `turn_finished` per top-level step with zero-cost usage, so `usage.json` turn accounting exercises its real path.
  - `runScenario(scenario, { mode: 'deterministic' | 'agentic', model?, auth? })`:
    1. Creates a temp `YANTRA_HOME` and calls `resetPathCache()` before and after, so no developer state leaks in either direction (memory → Testing).
    2. Starts `serveTaskSites()` and builds the scripted search provider and a recording `RankSignalSink`.
    3. Calls `runAgenticTask` with:
       - `profile` set to `resolveCommandTaskProfile(scenario.command, {})`, with an **empty env**, so `YANTRA_AGENT_RESEARCH_BROWSE` on a developer machine cannot change a baseline;
       - `ambient` carrying the location grant and `scenario.userLocation`;
       - `urlPolicyConfig: { requireHttps: false, maxUrlLength: 2048 }` (fixtures are plain HTTP);
       - `environmentLeaves` with an in-memory keychain, default ethics config (robots honored), an empty blocklist, host-mapped `createBrowserProvider` and `httpRequestFn`, and the scripted search resolver;
       - `rankSink`, `runStore` rooted in the temp home, and `createProvider` returning the `ScriptedAgentProvider` in deterministic mode, or omitted in agentic mode (the real provider).
    4. After the outcome resolves, reads every artifact tolerantly into `ScenarioRun` and closes the server.
  - JSONL readers report the line number of any unparseable line instead of throwing. FEAT-048's "every line parses" expectation measures that number.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - A two-step script (`web_fetch` of `article`, then `result_publish`) produces a `published` outcome. `tool-calls.jsonl` holds exactly two start and two end records, whose outputs deep-equal `auditProjectionOf` of the received results.
  - A `parallel` step of two `web_search` calls produces overlapping `startedAt` windows in the search call log.
  - A resolver returning `null` produces no tool call and one `unreachable` entry.
  - The developer's real `~/.yantra` is untouched (a canary file is unchanged), and `YANTRA_AGENT_RESEARCH_BROWSE=1` in `process.env` does not add browser tools.
  - A missing artifact reads as `null`.

### TASK-006: Expectation ledger with an owner ratchet

- [ ] **Implementation** (`expectations.ts`):
  - Matchers are small, typed, and printable: `equals`, `atLeast`, `atMost`, `includesAll`, `excludesAll`, `matchesShape`, `everyLine`, and `count`. Each renders a one-line description for failure output.
  - `assertExpectations(run, expectations)` produces **one Vitest test per expectation**, named `<scenario> › <owner> › <id>`, so CI lists each expectation individually, as the widget gauntlet does:
    - If `owner === 'current'` or the owner is not in `PENDING_OWNERS`, it asserts `target`.
    - If the owner is pending, it asserts `baseline`. It **also** evaluates `target`, and if `target` passes, it fails with "FEAT-0xx's target already holds; remove FEAT-0xx from PENDING_OWNERS and delete this baseline". A landed capability therefore cannot go unflipped.
  - Census assertions:
    - Every owner is one of the declared set.
    - Every pending owner has at least one expectation with a `baseline`.
    - A non-pending owner has none: a leftover baseline fails, naming the expectation.
    - `owner === 'current'` never carries a baseline.
    - Every expectation has a non-empty `note`.
  - A pinned baseline is a **characterization** of today's behavior, such as "the results page was fetched 3 times", "`records` is absent", or "the challenge page became a source". It is not a vague "fails". A baseline that crashes therefore fails loudly instead of passing vacuously. This is the FEAT-032 pattern ("preserved only as an explicit characterization for FEAT-034 to replace").
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - A synthetic pending expectation whose baseline holds and target fails passes.
  - One whose target holds fails with the flip message.
  - A non-pending expectation with a baseline fails the census.
  - Removing an owner from a synthetic `PENDING_OWNERS` switches the assertion to the target.
  - Matcher failure messages include the measured value.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the task-fidelity harness ("how an owning feature lands": remove it from `PENDING_OWNERS`, delete its baselines, and run the tier).
- **Verify**: `cd e2e && npx vitest run task-fidelity-harness -t "expectations"` passes.

### TASK-008: The outcome scorer

- [ ] **Implementation** (`score/scorer.ts`): pure functions of `(ScenarioRun, Scenario, TruthRow[])`. They read **only** public run artifacts plus the fixture request log, and tolerate every artifact a pre-FEAT-048/053 run lacks.
  - **Delivered rows.** The scorer extracts candidate rows from the published document in order of structure:
    1. `facets.comparison` rows;
    2. `sections[]` tables or bullets;
    3. findings;
    4. overview sentences.

    A delivered row is matched to a `TruthRow` when its unit contains the row key: the normalized title plus the seller, or a unique price-and-seller pair. Normalization lowercases, collapses whitespace, and strips currency formatting. Matching never uses fuzzy similarity, so scores are reproducible.

  - **`field_coverage`** = matched cells / (expected rows × required fields). Expected rows are the truth rows that satisfy every contract filter, capped at `contract.limit` after `contract.ranking`. A cell counts when the field value appears in the same unit as the row key, or in that row's comparison cell.
  - **`constraint_fidelity`** = 1 − violations / max(delivered rows, 1). Violations are:
    - delivered rows whose truth fails a filter;
    - each filter asserted in the title or overview without a `constraints[]` entry of `verified` (the "AWD offers" title case).

    `detail` names each violation.

  - **`source_fidelity`** = matched rows whose cited, or only, sources are on `contract.requiredSources` / matched rows. Off-contract hosts placed in the main answer are listed. Rows in a section labeled as alternatives are excluded once FEAT-053 provides that label.
  - **`citation_validity`** = cited claims whose cited source's stored evidence contains the value / cited claims. It is `null` when nothing is cited, which is today's baseline: every finding is editorial.
  - **`honesty`** = injected faults disclosed in notices / injected faults. Faults are the scripted search faults that fired, challenge fixtures fetched, and budget exhaustions in `run-health.json` or `runtime.jsonl`. A notice discloses a fault when its kind and source match the fault class. False claims about the site (the G2 "renders client-side" case) are out of scope for automation. They are listed in `detail` when the document asserts a cause no fault supports, as a heuristic that is reported, never scored.
  - **`cost`**: turns and tokens (`usage.json`, else the manifest's agent block), wall time (manifest), navigations (`run-health.json`, else counted from `tool-calls.jsonl`), browser launches (harness-counted), and fixture requests (server log).
  - **`interaction_required`**: the count of `INTERACTION_REQUIRED` codes in `tool-calls.jsonl` plus handoff outcomes.
  - **`stability`** (aggregate): the mean pairwise Jaccard similarity of the top-5 delivered row keys across runs, plus `same_top5_in_at_least`, the largest k such that k runs share an identical top-5 set. Plan §11's target is "same top-5 rows in ≥ 2 of 3 runs".

- [ ] **Unit Tests** (synthetic `ScenarioRun`s, no Chrome):
  - **The motivating shape.** A fixture-adapted reconstruction of run `20260925T130634Z`'s Brief (a price range, one seller from a snippet, six uncited findings, an "AWD" title, empty notices, and 11 injected search failures) scores near-zero coverage. It has one constraint violation ("asserted unverified"), `citation_validity: null`, and `honesty: 0/12`.
  - An oracle Brief with a full comparison table, `row_citations`, and verified constraints scores coverage 1.0, fidelity 1.0, and validity 1.0.
  - A row from an FWD item is counted as a violation.
  - An off-contract source in the answer lowers source fidelity.
  - A citation whose source lacks the value is invalid.
  - The stability of three identical runs is 1.0, and of three disjoint runs is 0.
  - Absent `run-health.json` or `usage.json` falls back as specified, with no throw.
  - Every score with a zero denominator is `null`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the task-fidelity harness (the scoring dimensions, their exact definitions, and what each cannot detect).
- **Verify**: `cd e2e && npx vitest run task-fidelity-harness -t "scorer"` passes.
- **Depends on**: TASK-005.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: The deterministic tier uses an in-memory keychain and never resolves a real secret. The agentic tier resolves model credentials exactly as the CLI does (`--auth-secret` or managed), and the harness never reads or prints a key. No consent, grant, or keychain behavior changes in production.
- **Error Handling**:
  - Harness infrastructure errors (egress outside the mapping, a fixture server that fails to bind, an unparseable artifact) are typed (`HarnessEgressError`, `HarnessSetupError`) and fail the scenario with the cause. They are never swallowed into a score.
  - An artifact the run did not produce reads as `null`, and the scorer treats it as "not measured", never as success.
  - The scripted search provider throws real core error classes, so the measured classification is production's classification.
- **Logging**: The harness adds no production log lines. Runs write their normal `runtime.jsonl` and `tool-calls.jsonl`, which the harness _reads_. `eval.ts` writes progress to stderr only, and `--json` stdout carries only the scorecard. No page text from fixtures appears in progress lines.
- **Security and privacy**:
  - The deterministic tier is hermetic: an egress guard covers both HTTP and Chrome, and fixtures live on a reserved TLD.
  - The environment-leaves seam replaces leaf dependencies only. Sanitizer, URL policy, ethics enforcement, budgets, consent, and audit stay non-bypassable and are composed by production code (memory → Architecture). A canary scan runs on every deterministic scenario.
  - The committed baseline is aggregate-only.
- **No website-specific logic**: Every fixture encodes a nameable generic pattern. Site names appear only in header provenance comments, enforced by a census that reuses the ESLint site-token list. Scoring rules key off structure (comparison rows, sections, notices), never a host.
- **Diagnostic cost**: The harness counts fetches and launches **outside** the code under test (the server log and the provider decorator). Its measurements therefore add no page read, fetch, or launch to the run (memory → Architecture: diagnostic work paid only where needed).
- **Compatibility**: No protocol or run-artifact format change. The scorecard is dev-only and versioned (`schema_version: 1`). `auditProjectionOf` and `environmentLeaves` are additive exports. Old run directories remain readable by the scorer.
- **Testing**:
  - Vitest AAA, real error classes, and `@no-llm` tags on the deterministic tier and harness self-tests.
  - Real Chrome only where a pattern requires a render.
  - Contention-sized timeouts.
  - Rebuild core and agent before trusting any e2e result.
  - The repo-wide lint/typecheck/e2e run is the final gate.
